grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Past progressive
grammarPoints.rule: Use was or were + verb-ing to talk about an action that was still going on at a moment in the past.

chart.title: Past progressive

intro_examples.text: By 250 CE, people were drinking hot chocolate.
intro_examples.jp: 西暦250年までに、人々はホットチョコレートを飲んでいました。

intro_examples.text: Was the cacao tree growing in Africa by then?

intro_examples.text: We were talking about the history of chocolate when I remembered the chocolate bar in my backpack.
intro_examples.jp: チョコレートの歴史について話していたとき、リュックの中の板チョコを思い出しました。

chart.note_rule: The past progressive is the background; the simple past is the thing that happens in front of it.
chart.note_exception: Use was with I/he/she/it, and were with you/we/they and plural nouns.
chart.note_exception_detail: Spelling: make → making (drop the e), stir → stirring (double the consonant), carry → carrying (keep the y).

table.title: was / were + verb-ing
notes: Use the past progressive for the longer, background action.
Use when + simple past for the short action that interrupts it.

grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Cause and effect with simple past and modals
grammarPoints.rule: Use so that + could or would to give the reason someone did something in the past.
grammarPoints.pattern: simple past clause + so that + subject + could / would + base verb

chart.title: Cause and effect with simple past and modals

intro_examples.text: The boy printed out the recipe so that he could read it while he was cooking.
intro_examples.jp: その男の子は料理しながら読めるようにレシピを印刷しました。

intro_examples.text: We put all the ingredients on the table so that it would be easy to find them later.
intro_examples.jp: あとで見つけやすいように、材料を全部テーブルに置きました。

intro_examples.text: The Aztecs added spices so that it would taste better.
intro_examples.jp: アステカの人々は、おいしくなるように香辛料を加えました。

rows.example: He printed the recipe so that he could read it.
rows.jp: 彼は読めるようにレシピを印刷しました。

rows.example: We put them on the table so that it would be easy.
rows.jp: 簡単になるように、それらをテーブルに置きました。

rows.example: We wore life jackets so that no one would have an accident.
rows.jp: 事故が起きないように救命胴衣を着けました。

rows.pattern: …so that + subject + could + take / drink / buy
rows.example: Some were buried with chocolate so that they could take it with them.
rows.jp: 持って行けるように、チョコレートとともに埋葬された人もいました。

rows.example: He showed me how to climb rocks, so that I can get stronger.
rows.jp: 強くなれるように、彼は岩の登り方を教えてくれました。

chart.note_rule: So that answers the question “why did they do it?” — it gives the purpose, not the time.
chart.note_exception: Use could for what someone was able to do, and would for what was expected to happen.
chart.note_exception_detail: The verb after could or would is always the base form: could read, would taste, wouldn't have.

notes: The base verb always follows could or would.
So that can be shortened to so in everyday speech.
